a3803.speaker: Professor Benyam Dawit Mezmur, deputy dean of postgraduate studies and head of the Children's Rights Project at the University of the Western Cape (UWC)
a3803.speech: While acknowledging that regional literature points to attempts at addressing climate change through sub-regional mechanisms, warned that climate change is a global challenge requiring synergised efforts ; encouraged delegates to engage critically with the seminar's programme, which attempts to move beyond the view of children as a homogeneous group: "Climate change affects children differently," he said, and warned against the temptation to see children as a monolith.

a3943.speaker: Ambassador Dr. Pindi Chana, Tanzanian Minister for Natural Resources and Tourism
a3943.speech: Emphasized that Tanzania can no longer rely solely on foreign aid and grants, and that the country must position itself as a strategic development partner in the global arena: “We must ensure we build a sustainable tourism sector that benefits all citizens. Despite the achievements made in increasing tourist arrivals and revenue, more efforts are needed to double those gains and ensure that communities benefit directly.”

a3943.speaker: Ambassador Dr. Pindi Chana, Tanzanian Minister for Natural Resources and Tourism
a3943.speech: Highlighting the country’s tourism potential: “Our country leads in the number of lions, leopards, and buffalos, and we rank third globally in terms of elephant population. We also boast rich cultural heritage, unmatched hospitality, beautiful beaches, marine biodiversity, and abundant lakes – all of which are critical assets for global tourism.”

a3943.speaker: Ambassador Dr. Pindi Chana, Tanzanian Minister for Natural Resources and Tourism
a3943.speech: Stressed that the workshop serves as a vital platform for exchanging ideas, perspectives, and expertise on conservation and tourism, urging the Ministry to intensify research in the sector to ensure the country benefits fully while preserving its natural resources.

a3943.speaker: Ambassador Dr. Pindi Chana, Tanzanian Minister for Natural Resources and Tourism
a3943.speech: “We should not become complacent with current successes, such as the rise in tourist arrivals from 1.7 million in 2021 to 5.3 million in 2024, and tourism revenue from USD 1.3bn US dollars to 3.9bn US dollars. We must work harder to achieve even greater milestones.”

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Has pledged to expedite efforts to resolve the European Union's concerns over illegal fishing activities which have earned Ghana a "Yellow Card" ; said lifting the ban was crucial because the ban significantly impacted industrial fishers, particularly those exporting tuna which contributed nearly $400 million annually to the economy ; “Illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing activities have earned Ghana a yellow card from the EU. The EU outlined several issues that need resolution for the yellow card to be lifted” ; said work had already begun in the ministry to address the issue, especially given the involvement of some fishing communities ; said the government was committed to aligning the country's fisheries regulations with international standards to restore compliance and secure the country's seafood exports to the EU market ; called for a review of the Fisheries Act 625, saying the bill previously submitted to Parliament had to be withdrawn and reworked to address gaps, particularly in inland fisheries and aquaculture ; “Addressing these challenges is vital to maintain this trade and secure foreign exchange for the country.”

a4062.speaker: Patrick Boamah, Member of Parliament for Okaikwei Central
a4062.speech: Asked a question on the EU's ban on the country, particularly the yellow card.

a4062.speaker: European Union
a4062.speech: Issued Ghana a yellow card as a formal warning for failing to effectively tackle illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing in its waters, and has indicated that continued non-compliance could escalate to a “red card,” effectively banning seafood exports to Europe.

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Responding to a suggestion on whether to promote solar-powered outboard motors as a viable alternative, stressed the need for a thorough scientific evaluation before implementing new technologies in the fisheries sector: “While I am open to exploring advanced technologies such as solar-powered motors, I believe we need to carefully assess their feasibility and benefits.”

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Responding to concerns about premix smuggling, indicated her readiness to explore innovative approaches to ensure proper distribution and eliminate smuggling when approved as minister for the sector.

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Announced plans to establish a Blue Economy Commission, which would operate alongside the existing Fisheries Commission and Premix Secretariat under the ministry ; said this new body would differ from the Fisheries Commission, which primarily served as a regulator, and would focus on policy development, research, and fostering innovation in the fisheries and aquaculture industries ; “The Blue Economy Commission will examine how we can expand fisheries beyond its narrow scope. This includes fisheries, bioprospecting, seabed mining and other ocean-related activities.”

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Responding to how illegal mining activities affect rivers resulting in mercury contamination and declining fish stocks, said that would require an intersectoral approach involving multiple ministries such as Fisheries, Environment, Lands, Transport, and Science and Technology, and would also require a cabinet-level task force; said when approved she would collaborate with relevant ministries to address these issues comprehensively.

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Reaffirmed her commitment to the NDC's fisheries policy as outlined in the party's manifesto ; said aquaculture was a vital component of the NDC's fisheries policy as it provided 60 per cent of Ghanaians' protein needs ; indicated that marine and inland fish resources were depleting, adding that “Currently, Ghana has only about six large-scale aquaculture farms, 14 medium-scale farms, and over 2,300 small-scale operations” ; said her administration was committed to supporting, attracting, and facilitating funding for operators of aquaculture farms and that the ministry would collaborate with other stakeholders, especially the Ministry of Agriculture, to explore and increase local production of maize and soybean to reduce the high cost of fish feed.

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: On how to create opportunities for women in the fishing sector, said that through the establishment of the Women's Development Bank the ministry would be able to provide small loans for fishmongers to improve their work ; said her administration aimed to set up processing centres, adding that “In the area of aquaculture, we envision significant investments in creating aquaculture farms equipped with cold storage facilities, refrigerated vans, and market linkages to bring suppliers and buyers together” ; said the sector was women-dominated, adding that “While men own most of the canoes, some women also own them” ; “Women play a significant role in the value chain by smoking, frying, and preparing the fish” ; indicated that her administration would rebuild markets to support women in the fisheries industry to enable them to become more economically and socially empowered.

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Assured the committee that her administration would be fair and equitable to anyone deserving of a licence: “Anyone deserving of a licence after following due process will receive one. However, we will also need to manage our resources carefully to prevent congestion in the sector.”

a4062.speaker: Emelia Arthur, Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture of Ghana
a4062.speech: Said she would want to be remembered as the Fisheries Minister under whose tenure fisheries production increased ; “I also want to be remembered for integrating indigenous knowledge with scientific approaches to improve the sector” ; said she would like to be remembered for being a minister who operationalised the long-awaited Fisheries College, which began in 2013.

a4305.speaker: Senator Abubakar Kyari, Nigerian Minister of Agriculture and Food Security (represented by Dr. Deola-Tayo Lordbanjou, Director of the Federal Department of Agricultural Extension Services)
a4305.speech: Called for the creation of agricultural insurance and weather advisory desks at the community level to enhance adaptation and resilience to climate change by smallholder farmers; said this would promote a sustainable environment for agricultural investment; pointed out that making weather advisory services available at the right time at the community level would reduce the effect of climate change on the agricultural ecosystem and boost production ; “The importance of insurance cover for farmers cannot be over-emphasised as this can help to protect investments, increase productivity as well as livelihoods of farmers which will in turn aid the country achieve its food security objectives” ; “there is also the growing frequency and severity of flood, drought, and other environmental disasters arising from climate change. Farmers are particularly vulnerable to these disasters, and it sets them back each time they occur by wiping off their investments” ; revealed that “the Ministry has resolved to develop the agricultural sector towards the attainment of the objectives of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) especially those of zero hunger and to improve sustainable agricultural practices” ; stressed that “agricultural investments must be protected and market-oriented for us to be able to move away from the subsistence farming being practised by our smallholder farmers.”

a4305.speaker: Senator Abubakar Kyari, Nigerian Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a4305.speech: Lauded the USAID for its tireless efforts in strengthening social stability through social services and promotion of a more market-led economy that has enhanced Nigeria’s capacity as a responsible regional and trade partner.

a4305.speaker: Jean-Pierre Rousseau, Director, Winrock International
a4305.speech: Stated that agriculture insurance and weather advisory services have tremendous potential to transform the agricultural sector in Nigeria; pledged that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Feed the Future Programme would continue to support the agricultural sector in Nigeria.

a4444.speaker: Alex Majogoro, Acting Director of the Nelico organisation
a4444.speech: Reading the annual report of the NGOs in Geita region, said that as a result of the decision by the President of the United States, Donald Trump, to suspend 90 percent of funding through USAID, many organisations have been destabilised ; "Apart from the suspension of the PEPFAR programme, other projects that have been halted include campaigns to fight Malaria as well as basic health services," said Majogoro ; He said many organisations depend on funding from international donors, so the absence of those funds has caused a decline in health services, the halting of some development projects and a large gap in the areas that had depended on that aid ; He said some organisations in the region have been forced to cut staff by more than 50 percent, while others have had to reduce employees' salaries to cope with dependence on funding.

a4444.speaker: NaCONGO (National Council of NGOs)
a4444.speech: According to NaCONGO, many organisations, especially the newer ones, have failed to carry out their responsibilities, while others have closed their offices due to lack of funding.

a4444.speaker: Paulina Alex, regional chairperson of NaCONGO in Geita
a4444.speech: Said that despite those challenges, the non-governmental organisations have succeeded in implementing various interventions, including child protection and human rights, the fight against harmful traditional practices and child marriage, the fight against drugs, health, education, the environment, and legal aid ; She said more than 50 projects have been implemented in Geita region and more than 300 groups of women and youth have been economically empowered through loans ; "Through these organisations, more than 10 health centres have been renovated and equipped. 480 citizens have been given legal aid, but also in the employment sector, these 70 organisations present here in our region have provided jobs to 500 people," said Alex.

a4444.speaker: Statistics/data on NGO investment (cited)
a4444.speech: Statistics show that non-governmental organisations invested 7.2 billion shillings in the year 2024/25 in the health, education, agriculture, social welfare, environment and gender-based-violence sectors.

a4444.speaker: Deodatus Kayango, Representative of the Geita Regional Commissioner
a4444.speech: Opening the meeting, stressed the importance of cooperation between the Government and those organisations, saying, "The Government recognises the great work being done by NGOs in bringing development to the citizens." ; He said the aim of the meeting was to meet with all the non-governmental organisations in order to discuss together various issues for improving services and strengthening cooperation in implementing projects and social services.

a4444.speaker: Deodatus Kayango, Representative of the Geita Regional Commissioner
a4444.speech: Speaking about the general election expected in October this year, called on the organisations authorised to provide civic education to citizens to take patriotism into account: "We are heading towards an election. Non-governmental organisations that have been granted permission to provide education, provide civic education while taking patriotism into account. If civic education is provided well, society will gain good awareness and will turn out to elect good leaders," said Kayango.

a4556.speaker: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
a4556.speech: According to OPEC Secretariat calculations, the price of the OPEC basket of 12 crudes stood at $75.11 a barrel on Monday, March 24, 2025, compared with $74.91 the previous day.

a4686.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a4686.speech: Described relations between Dakar and Ankara as opening “new prospects for strategic cooperation”; said the visit constitutes “a decisive stage” in relations between the two countries; expressed his “deep gratitude” to President Erdogan, his wife and the Turkish people for “their welcome marked by warmth and fraternity”; concluded by stressing the two nations’ shared commitment to work for “a future founded on peace, shared prosperity and solidarity.”

a4686.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a4686.speech: Encouraged Turkish companies to diversify their investments beyond the construction sector and presented the “Senegal 2050” National Transformation Programme.

a4686.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, President of Turkey
a4686.speech: Highlighted Senegal as a key partner of Turkey in West Africa.

a4686.speaker: Cevdet Yilmaz, Vice-President of Turkey
a4686.speech: Stressed that President Faye’s official visit would intensify trade relations; also recalled the signing the previous day in Ankara of a Memorandum of Understanding establishing a High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council between the Republic of Turkey and the Republic of Senegal, which opens “great opportunities for our entrepreneurs.”

a4686.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye and Recep Tayyip Erdogan (joint)
a4686.speech: The two heads of state concluded their meeting with a call for a reform of international institutions for a more equitable world order.

a4777.speaker: Old Mutual Malawi Limited (statement)
a4777.speech: Has unveiled a five-point survival plan to help individuals navigate turbulent economic times, particularly in the face of potential job losses.

a4777.speaker: Benard Chiluzi, Old Mutual Malawi Limited financial education manager
a4777.speech: Said while the stop order could be temporary, it is important to prepare for any potential long-term impacts such as job losses and increased stress; said at Old Mutual Malawi they understand the importance of financial resilience during uncertain times, hence providing five survival tips.

a4777.speaker: Benard Chiluzi, Old Mutual Malawi Limited financial education manager
a4777.speech: Said the affected people should prioritise needs over wants and focus on essentials such as food, rent, utilities and school fees for dependents: “Temporarily reduce spending on entertainment, dining out and luxury items. Furthermore, track expenses by using a simple budget tracker to monitor expenditure and identify areas to cut back” ; said there is a need to start saving to cover basic expenses in case of job loss or income delay, and to automate the transfer of savings into an instrument that brings growth to the invested money, citing investment options through Old Mutual Unit Trust ; said this is also the time to think of starting a small business to generate additional income ; said the fourth survival tip is to negotiate with lenders for more flexible repayment terms or lower interest rates ; said because financial challenges affect the entire household, there is a need to have an open conversation with the family about the situation and explore ways everyone can contribute to cutting costs.

a4899.speaker: USAID (statement on social media)
a4899.speech: “We congratulate more than 1,000 South Sudanese youths aged 15-29 who graduated on October 31 after completing more than six months of USAID’s Youth Empowerment training in Jur River, Wau, Akobo, and Budi Counties.” ; “They learned foundational literacy and entrepreneurial skills. Now they can read, write, and have the basic skills to start a business.”

a4899.speaker: Education Development Center (EDC), the activity’s technical lead
a4899.speech: According to EDC, the basic literacy training has improved access to knowledge and skills among young people aged between 15 and 29.

a4928.speaker: Doreen Bogdan-Martin, Secretary-General of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
a4928.speech: Declared that it is “in our collective interest to shape AI faster than it shapes us.”

a5302.speaker: Jude Law, British actor
a5302.speech: said Sunday he became an "obsessive" watcher of Vladimir Putin as he prepared for his role as the Russian leader in his new film "The Wizard of the Kremlin". "There's a lot of footage one could watch and, personally when I start going down that rabbit hole, it becomes sort of obsessive," he told a press conference. "You're looking for ever more, newer material." ; He said portraying Putin had been a challenge because of his famously deadpan expression. "The tricky side to me was that the public face that we see (of Putin), we see very, very little. There's this mask." ; Law insisted he had not aimed for an "impersonation" of Putin and credited the likeness to "an amazing makeup and hair team."

a5302.speaker: Olivier Assayas, French director
a5302.speech: insisted he wanted Law "to appropriate the character" and become "a vessel for what he represents."

a5302.speaker: Olivier Assayas, French director
a5302.speech: said it was first and foremost a story about authoritarianism, with Russia's transition from a chaotic democracy in the late 1990s to Putin's modern autocracy a warning for the West. "We made a movie about what politics has become and the very scary and dangerous situation we all feel we are in," he explained.

a5302.speaker: Jim Jarmusch, independent American director
a5302.speech: has called ["Father Mother Sister Brother"] "a kind of anti-action film", featuring three separate dysfunctional families in conversation in the rural north-east of the United States, Dublin and Paris.

a5302.speaker: The Hollywood Reporter
a5302.speech: called the Netflix-funded production [Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein"] "epic-scale storytelling of uncommon beauty, feeling and artistry".

a5302.speaker: Variety
a5302.speech: saying the film "cost more than 'Titanic' and still looks like it was made for TV".

a5302.speaker: Open letter (from film industry figures ahead of the festival)
a5302.speech: denouncing the Israeli government and calling on the festival to speak out more forcefully [on the Gaza war].

a5302.speaker: Reports (unattributed media reports)
a5302.speech: according to reports, the production ["The Voice of Hind Rajab"] has attracted heavyweight Hollywood support from Brad Pitt, Jonathan Glazer and Joaquin Phoenix who have joined as executive producers.

a5636.speaker: Police sources (The Gambia)
a5636.speech: According to police sources, the two young men were released without charge on Sunday, April 20, after two nights in police custody, on orders from higher authorities, with no formal charges filed.

a5636.speaker: Anonymous source close to the matter
a5636.speech: Told Alkamba Times that fears of international backlash influenced the decision: “The authorities didn’t want the case to escalate to court. There are concerns it could provoke reactions from international partners and potentially jeopardize foreign aid.”

a5636.speaker: Gambia Police (police statement)
a5636.speech: Described the investigation as probing an “unnatural sex offense” but offered no further comment.

a5636.speaker: Sheikh Omar Bah, prominent local imam
a5636.speech: Condemned the act, stating, “Homosexuality is against our faith and traditions. The government must uphold our values.”

a5636.speaker: Banjul-based human rights activist (anonymous)
a5636.speech: Criticized the arrests, saying, “Arresting people for their private conduct violates human rights. This shows we’re still far from respecting individual freedoms.”

a5636.speaker: Social media user on X (trending post)
a5636.speech: “We are a Muslim nation, and such acts are unacceptable. The police did right to act.”

a5636.speaker: Another social media user on X
a5636.speech: Cautioned, “Releasing them was wise. We can’t afford to lose aid over this.”

a5636.speaker: Government of The Gambia (non-response)
a5636.speech: The government has not issued an official statement on the release.

a5640.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana
a5640.speech: Has urged African leaders to tackle corruption as a critical step toward economic transformation; highlighted how corruption continues to erode Africa’s economic potential and stall progress; warned that corruption remains a persistent obstacle to sustainable development: “Prosperity cannot be achieved without good governance, transparency, and accountability. Investors and businesses thrive where there is stability, predictable policies, and the rule of law.” ; Lamented that despite Africa’s commitment to democratic governance, corruption has undermined trust in institutions and stunted economic progress: “Our youth are tired and frustrated at the lack of opportunities to realise their dreams and aspirations. Our decision to embrace democratic governance was supposed to yield a dividend that would improve the lives of our people and bring prosperity to all. Unfortunately, progress has been sluggish and intangible.” ; Stressed that the success of initiatives like the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) depends on eliminating corruption-related inefficiencies that hinder trade and investment.

a5640.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana
a5640.speech: Urged African leaders to move beyond rhetoric and take decisive action to fight corruption: “The decisions we make at this conference must not end in resolutions alone. We must act with urgency, determination, and a shared vision for prosperity.” ; Called for collective responsibility in eliminating corruption and ensuring that Africa’s resources serve the greater good.

a5640.speaker: Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana’s first President (quoted by Mahama)
a5640.speech: “The forces that unite us are intrinsic and greater than the superimposed influences that keep us apart.”

a5644.speaker: South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (statement)
a5644.speech: Said South Korea detected the two launches from a western coastal town, just north of the North Korean capital, on Monday morning.

a5644.speaker: KCNA / North Korea’s state news agency
a5644.speech: Said two projectiles were fired from a multiple rocket launcher, aiming at targets 395km and 337km away, respectively: “The 600mm multiple rocket launcher mobilised in the firing … is a means of tactical nuclear weapon,” capable of “paralysing” an enemy airfield.

a5644.speaker: Japan (Ministry of Defence)
a5644.speech: Detected the launches, saying two ballistic missiles were fired at about 7am local time on Monday, reaching an altitude of approximately 100km and 50km and travelling between 350km and 400km before falling outside Japan’s Exclusive Economic Zone ; said it would continue to gather and analyse information in close cooperation with the United States ; “North Korea’s series of actions, including its repeated ballistic missile launches, threaten the peace and security of Japan, the region, and the international community. Japan lodged a strong protest and forcefully condemned North Korea.”

a5644.speaker: Kim Yo Jong, Kim Jong Un’s sister (statement)
a5644.speech: Issued a warning against any increased US presence on the Korean peninsula: “We are carefully examining the influence it would exert on the security of our state” ; “The frequency of using the Pacific as our firing range depends upon the US forces’ action character.”

a5644.speaker: North Korea’s state media
a5644.speech: Said on Sunday the ICBM test was meant to further bolster its “fatal” nuclear attack capacity and verify the weapon’s reliability, as well as the combat readiness of the country’s nuclear force.

a5644.speaker: South Korea and the US
a5644.speech: Say their military drills are defensive in nature.

a5644.speaker: Pyongyang (North Korea)
a5644.speech: Portrays the drills as a rehearsal for invasion.

a5644.speaker: Park Won-gon, professor at Ewha Womans University in Seoul
a5644.speech: Said Monday’s missile launch and statement echoed the North Korean foreign ministry’s recent threat to take “unprecedentedly persistent, strong” responses to the allies’ joint military drills.

a5644.speaker: North Korean foreign ministry
a5644.speech: Recently threatened to take “unprecedentedly persistent, strong” responses to the allies’ joint military drills.

a5787.speaker: A peacebuilding practitioner (anonymous, interviewed for the authors' research)
a5787.speech: “Humanitarians are a nightmare to work with.”

a5787.speaker: Yearly UN-backed humanitarian response plans for Somalia (documents cited)
a5787.speech: A quick glance shows the scale of the problem: humanitarian funding may double or halve from year to year – dramatic swings that constitute 10-20% of Somalia’s gross domestic product. In 2017, for example, humanitarian funding doubled from the previous year; in 2023, it was cut in half.

a5787.speaker: Donors
a5787.speech: Donors say they’re trying to prevent famine.

a5787.speaker: Many Somali civil society actors
a5787.speech: The position of many Somali civil society actors is clear: The government is critical to ensuring coherent and sustainable peace, development, and ultimately, the alleviation of humanitarian need.

a5787.speaker: The Nexus Consortium in Somalia (platform of eight Somali organisations)
a5787.speech: Is one of many actors continuing to advocate for this systemic shift [renewed attention towards the state], yet substantive change remains elusive.

a5842.speaker: Angela Merkel, former German Chancellor
a5842.speech: Has told the BBC the gas deals she made with Russia were intended to help German firms and kept the peace with Moscow. She tells the BBC she had two motives with the pipelines: German business interests but also maintaining peaceful links with Russia. She says she did everything in her power to ensure peaceful means of co-operation with Russia. Mrs Merkel insists she tried to curb Russian attacks on Ukraine using diplomacy and negotiations, which - she admits - ultimately failed. A new era in Europe's relations with Russia "regrettably" began following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, says Mrs Merkel.

a5842.speaker: Angela Merkel, former German Chancellor
a5842.speech: Insisted the war with Ukraine would have started earlier if she hadn't blocked Kyiv's entry into Nato in 2008. She says she believes the war in Ukraine would have started sooner and would likely have been worse, if Kyiv had begun the path to Nato membership in 2008. "We would have seen military conflict even earlier. It was completely clear to me that President Putin would not have stood idly by and watched Ukraine join Nato." ; "And back then, Ukraine as a country would certainly not have been as prepared as it was in February 2022."

a5842.speaker: Angela Merkel, former German Chancellor
a5842.speech: Expresses concern about Vladimir Putin's renewed threats of using nuclear weapons. "We must do everything possible to prevent the use of nuclear weapons." ; "Thankfully, China also spoke about this a while back. We shouldn't be paralysed by fear, but we must also acknowledge that Russia is the biggest, or alongside the US, one of the two biggest nuclear powers in the world." ; "The potential is frightening."

a5842.speaker: Angela Merkel, former German Chancellor
a5842.speech: Admits the AfD made big gains, but she makes no apology for her political decisions. As for suggestions that her 2015 policies helped fuel anti-immigration and far-right parties elsewhere too, Mrs Merkel says she can't be held responsible for all of Europe. The only way to combat the far right is to stop illegal migration, she says. She calls on Europe's leaders to invest more in African nations to improve standards of living there, so fewer people will be tempted to leave their homes.

a5842.speaker: Angela Merkel, former German Chancellor
a5842.speech: On handling Donald Trump: "It's really important to know what your priorities are, to present them clearly and not to be scared, because Donald Trump can be very outspoken." ; "He expresses himself very clearly. And if you do that, there is a certain mutual respect. That was my experience anyway."

a5842.speaker: Angela Merkel, former German Chancellor
a5842.speech: Asked if she misses all that power and politics, her swift answer is: "No, not at all."

a5842.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a5842.speech: Disagrees. He describes Mrs Merkel's Nato decision, backed by then-French President Nicolas Sarkozy, as a clear "miscalculation" that emboldened Russia.

a5842.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a5842.speech: Described that cheap gas as a geopolitical tool of the Kremlin.

a5842.speaker: Matteo Renzi, former Italian premier
a5842.speech: Says she was the de-facto leader of Europe - "the boss of the European Union". "Do you remember when [former US Secretary of State] Henry Kissinger used to say 'what is the telephone number of Europe?'. My answer was: clearly, the mobile number of Angela Merkel." He adds that when judging the Merkel legacy - over Russia and otherwise - it is important to remember the norms of the time. "One cannot attack Angela for the relations with Russia. In 2005, 2006 [they] were a goal of everyone in Europe, not only a goal of Angela Merkel."

a5842.speaker: Radoslaw Fogiel, Polish MP
a5842.speech: Said German gas money filled Russia's war chest - used to fund the invasion of Ukraine.

a5842.speaker: Barack Obama, US President
a5842.speech: Praised her as a courageous and moral leader.

a5889.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a5889.speech: Stated that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funded terrorist organizations, including Boko Haram.

a5889.speaker: Nigerian scholars (Professors Kyari Mohammed, Jibrin Ibrahim, Usman Tar and Chris Kwaja, Dr. Atta Barkindo, Abdulbasit Kassim and others)
a5889.speech: Have extensively researched and reported the origins and evolution of Boko Haram.

a5889.speaker: Experts on the subject matter
a5889.speech: Are sharply divided: some see Perry's thesis as political, while others hold it as something to interrogate.

a5998.speaker: Steven Cheung, White House communications director
a5998.speech: Confirmed the meeting and said that the two men "met privately and had a very productive discussion" ; added: "More details about the meeting will follow."

a5998.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5998.speech: Said on social media, shortly after arriving in Rome on Friday, that Ukraine and Russia should meet for "high-level talks" on ending Moscow's war, which is now in its fourth year.

a5998.speaker: EuroNews
a5998.speech: Reported as the source for the White House communications director's account of the meeting.

a6139.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States (executive order)
a6139.speech: In an executive order made public this Friday, ordered government officials to prioritise the resettlement of white South Africans through the American refugee programme, which he suspended on the very first day of his term ; also orders an end to all American aid to South Africa: the US development aid agency USAID - in the process of being dissolved - must immediately end every assistance programme in South Africa.

a6139.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6139.speech: Accused the South African government of discriminating against “Afrikaners”, the descendants of European settlers, mainly originating from the Netherlands, who arrived in the country in the 1600s and who imposed, in the 20th century, the system of racial segregation known as apartheid.

a6139.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6139.speech: According to experts, Afrikaners and other whites are a “privileged” minority in South Africa, having retained their economic dominance over the highly industrialised country, rich in mineral resources.

a6139.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire of South African origin and adviser to Trump
a6139.speech: Alleges that white South Africans are now “the target of oppression by the country's government”, citing a law which, according to American conservatives such as Trump's adviser and billionaire Elon Musk, authorises the seizure of land belonging to white South Africans.

a6178.speaker: Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), statement issued by Comrade Jamilu Aliyu Charanchi, National Coordinator
a6178.speech: Strongly condemned the continued detention of minors by the Police and demanded their immediate release; said the Coalition has observed that a number of Nigerians, sadly many minors below the age of 18, have been detained for over 90 days before their arraignment in an Abuja High Court last Friday for exercising their constitutional rights in a protest against hunger and bad governance; said it learnt that at least four of the children collapsed in the courtroom during the arraignment as a result of hunger and absence of medical care while in custody ; "Unfortunately, the detention and arraignment of those frail, malnourished and hapless children have exposed the government as a desperate entity that is determined to de-market and embarrass Nigeria before the international community while presenting its credentials for medals in gross inhumanity." ; "The continued detention and mistreatment of these minors is a gross violation of their basic rights, including the right to freedom of expression and assembly." ; "CNG strongly condemns this abuse of power and the blatant disregard for the welfare and dignity of young citizens." ; "The treatment these children are receiving highlights a troubling failure of state actors to prioritize the welfare and rights of its most vulnerable citizens, children, especially when their 'crime' was to demand better governance and accountability." ; "It is disheartening that in a country with a history of resilience and promise, minors are being made to endure starvation and harsh conditions while awaiting trial for daring to speak up for their future." ; "This is not only a violation of domestic law but also contravenes international human rights principles protecting children from harm and unlawful detention." ; "Ideally, those children are supposed to be treated first as victims of state abuse and deprivation whose leaders have failed to provide the necessary leadership that can mold them into better members of the society as they are a direct outcome of our decayed system." ; "It is shamefully despicable that criminals and bandits that are holding the entire country to ransom do not face such stringent consequences for their actions."

a6178.speaker: Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), statement issued by Comrade Jamilu Aliyu Charanchi, National Coordinator
a6178.speech: On governance and the economy: "Evidently, the Government has consistently proven that people's problems and deteriorating situations are not part of its priority because of its disregard for the daily hardships of its citizens." ; "Increasingly, frequent blackouts have become a norm across the country, severely impacting homes, businesses, and essential services which became worse with the recent blackout." ; "The elimination of fuel subsidies and constant raising of fuel prices have pushed the cost of living to record highs, making basic necessities even harder to afford. Instead of prioritizing the welfare of the populace by providing feasible alternatives or relief, the government's priorities appear to be detaining, abusing and crushing the vulnerable children that need support and protection to grow into responsible adults." ; "Unfortunately, hunger and starvation have become weapons against defenseless and malnourished teenagers." ; "It is clear that the government's neglect of essential services and its catastrophic economic policies have strangulated millions in a state of uncertainty, desperation, and disillusionment in which these minors belong." ; "These children must not be targeted as the scapegoat for expressing their frustrations as Nigerians have never gone through such dehumanizing and cruel policies that this administration promotes."

a6178.speaker: Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), statement issued by Comrade Jamilu Aliyu Charanchi, National Coordinator
a6178.speech: Called for the immediate and unconditional release of all minors detained for participating in the protests, adding that "We demand that the government prioritize dialogue and constructive engagement over intimidation, especially with young citizens who represent the future of this nation." ; "In the interim, we urge relevant agencies and civil society organizations to provide immediate humanitarian assistance to these detained children to mitigate further health risks." ; "The protection of children is non-negotiable, and we implore the authorities to treat these young citizens with the compassion and respect they deserve."

a6561.speaker: Justin Brady, Head of Office of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in Somalia
a6561.speech: "Somalia's coping mechanisms are significantly less than those of the neighbouring countries. Therefore, the impact [of floods, locusts and COVID-19] is not simply humanitarian but has the potential to reverse some of the political and security gains that the international community has invested in over the past decade." ; "We need to continue to work together and expand the coordination with the private sector, civil society and have more engagement with the diaspora." ; Mr. Brady said the UN's warning takes into account Somalia's inherent structural weaknesses, which make the country far more vulnerable than the other countries in the region, and calls for an "all hands on deck approach to avert the worst."

a6561.speaker: Justin Brady, Head of Office of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in Somalia
a6561.speech: On the flood response: "The UN has been deploying shelter and non-food items as well as looking at the potential for infectious diseases such as acute watery diarrhea, cholera and malnutrition that often emerge during the time of floods."

a6561.speaker: Justin Brady, Head of Office of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in Somalia
a6561.speech: On the locust threat: "We have a situation of the two problems of floods and COVID-19 converging and reinforcing the impact on the population, and then we have the locusts. We expect to see a portion of the crops this year lost to the locust infestation, which will compound the food security and nutrition situation for many Somalis."

a6561.speaker: Abdikarim Hussein Abdi, Programme Manager for Development Action Network, a local NGO
a6561.speech: "We have about 240,000 people who were displaced from their homes. The floods submerged people's markets and businesses, thereby leaving many people without any source of income. Commodity prices have skyrocketed, harvests have been destroyed and the little food coming to the market is too expensive."

a6561.speaker: Hawa Gedi, a mother of four displaced by floods at the Ceel Jaale camp for internally displaced persons in Belet Weyne
a6561.speech: Asked for more help for the many families whose livelihoods were destroyed: "I was displaced from Bula Qodah by floods and settled here at Ceel Jaale. We are grateful to the humanitarian agencies for providing us with water and other basic needs, but we need more support. We need food. We have nothing to eat."

a6561.speaker: Malyun Mohammed, a beauty shop-owner in Baidoa, South West State
a6561.speech: "Coronavirus has affected our business. Three or four people cannot enter the shop at once, so we now serve customers one-by-one. Added to that, there is no port in Baidoa so we rely on supplies from Mogadishu and Dubai but flights were suspended so many of our businesses are at a standstill."

a6561.speaker: Etienne Peterschmitt, FAO Country Representative in Somalia
a6561.speech: Believes that the impact of the current desert locust outbreak in Somalia could, by September 2020, increase the number of Somalis facing food insecurity or severe hunger by half a million.

a6561.speaker: OCHA and WHO
a6561.speech: Have described the floods, locusts and COVID-19 as an unprecedented "triple threat," which needed adequate funding to fight against.

a6561.speaker: Dr. Mamunur Rahman Malik, WHO Country Representative for Somalia
a6561.speech: "Unless we are able to rapidly scale up our response operations, unless we get adequate funding from our donors, we will not be able to respond to this need of the government and that window is closing very rapidly." ; "What we are seeing in Somalia is cases remain undiagnosed, undetected, the self-isolation and quarantine measures are not working as efficiently as we expect them to work."

a6561.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6561.speech: According to WHO, the funding gaps are in the areas of case management, surveillance and laboratory diagnostics and coordination. Without this, the response to COVID-19 is hampered.

a6742.speaker: Mohamud Moallim Abdulle, Commissioner of Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA), and Ahmed Juma Al-Rumaithi, UAE Ambassador to Somalia
a6742.speech: During the meeting, both officials reaffirmed enhancing bilateral ties in the fields of humanitarian assistance, particularly ways to deliver emergency aid to the people affected by the drought in the northern region of the country. The two sides agreed the need to deliver emergency aid and tackle the drought that has affected the people in those areas.

a6742.speaker: Mohamud Moallim Abdulle, Commissioner of Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a6742.speech: The Commissioner informed the Ambassador of his visit to the UAE, and that he intends to have a meeting with the Humanitarian and Emergency Agencies.

a6742.speaker: Ahmed Juma Al-Rumaithi, UAE Ambassador to Somalia
a6742.speech: the Ambassador expects the humanitarian support to be increased ; Ambassador Ahmed vowed that the Emirate Government will work very closely with the agency and will soon deliver a shipment of aid to the people facing humanitarian issues in Somalia.

a6826.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a6826.speech: Spoke of the American government’s support for the country, including the Global Fund, the US Agency for International Development (USAID) and the World Food Programme (WFP); according to the Ministry of Finance, he recalled that part of that support remains suspended by decision of Donald Trump, but assured that he is working for the continuity of support in areas crucial for the country.

a6826.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a6826.speech: Asked about the government’s new institutional structure.

a6826.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Mozambique
a6826.speech: According to the Ministry of Finance, Vrooman recalled that part of the US support remains suspended by decision of Donald Trump, while assuring he is working for the continuity of support in crucial areas.

a6826.speaker: Carla Loveira, Mozambican Minister of Finance
a6826.speech: Commented that the current situation of suspended funding creates imbalances in the proposal for the 2025 Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOE).

a6826.speaker: Carla Loveira, Mozambican Minister of Finance
a6826.speech: “In answer to the question, the finance minister assured that it is centred on three main areas: the restructuring of the government machinery; fiscal consolidation; and good governance.”

a6826.speaker: Carla Loveira, Mozambican Minister of Finance
a6826.speech: Welcomed the Spanish government’s openness to continuing to support Mozambique and the invitation extended for the country’s participation in the Conference, since the country is a signatory of the 2030 Agenda and has been taking part in the reform of the international financial architecture.

a6826.speaker: Teresa Orjales, Ambassador of Spain to Mozambique
a6826.speech: Showed her country’s openness to continuing to support Mozambique in its development policies and spoke of the 4th International Conference on Financing for Development, to be held in Seville, Spain, from 30 June to 3 July 2025: “This conference will be an opportunity to accelerate the implementation of the 2030 Agenda. It will also support the reform of the international financial architecture, will likewise define the global financing agenda and advance the sustainable development goals.”

a7009.speaker: Aviation unions (Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, National Union of Air Transport Employees and Association of Nigerian Aviation Professionals) (joint statement)
a7009.speech: Raised concerns over repeated assaults on Aviation Security (AVSEC) personnel by Nigeria Customs Service operatives, demanding immediate intervention; issued a 14-day ultimatum for the redeployment of the Controller, Murtala Muhammed Area Command of the customs in charge of Pilgrims and Cargo Terminal, alongside all officers involved; called on the federal government to redefine Customs' roles within bonded warehouses in civil aviation, saying there was the need for alignment with global standards; demanded a reduction in the number of Customs personnel at airports in line with international best practices; urged the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria to establish a Memorandum of Understanding with paramilitary agencies, saying this would clarify operational scopes and prevent future conflicts; and warned of potential industrial unrest if their demands are not met within the stipulated time frame.

a7009.speaker: Abdullahi Maiwada, National Public Relations Officer, Nigeria Customs Service
a7009.speech: Said "A miscommunication regarding equipment movement and seating arrangements resulted in a disagreement between officials of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and officers of the NCS."

a7009.speaker: Nigeria Customs Service (statement)
a7009.speech: Stated that the Skyway Aviation Handling Company (SAHCOL) and the Nigerian Aviation Handling Company (NAHCO) are Customs licensed Customs Bonded Warehouses: "While the Service continues to engage constructively with all relevant stakeholders to strengthen operational protocols and to uphold the collective national interest, it is essential to reiterate that the NAHCO and SAHCO Import & Export Warehouses are licensed Customs Bonded Warehouses operating in full compliance with Section 122 of the Nigeria Customs Service Act, 2023. As stipulated in Section 127 of the Act, these warehouses remain under the control of the NCS."

a7009.speaker: Group Capt. John Ojikutu (rtd), aviation security analyst
a7009.speech: Called for the intervention of the National Security Council to solve the recurring problem: "It's our negligence for not complying with ICAO Annex 17. 3.1.6. Set up a National Aviation Security Committee and not CIVIL Aviation Security Committee. We've been talking about this in the last twenty five years but those in the administration of our government prefer their solutions with Multiple Security Agencies without a Unified Command and Control over the government security agencies working in the Airports."

a7027.speaker: Head Coach Sallah, Team Gambia athletics head coach
a7027.speech: Praised the athletes' commitment and determination; acknowledged the disqualifications were tough to take, but said the performances showed the growing standard of Gambian athletics ; “The experience gained on this international stage will be invaluable as the athletes continue their development.”

a7027.speaker: Gina Mariam Bass Bittaye, Gambian sprinter
a7027.speech: Speaking after the race, said she was pleased with the result despite the cold weather ; “Qualification was the priority in the opening round, not speed.”

a7027.speaker: Isatou Sey, Gambian sprinter
a7027.speech: Blamed the weather but called the experience valuable ; “Competing at the Games has been a great learning experience.”

a7027.speaker: Ebrima Camara, Gambian sprinter
a7027.speech: Reflected on a tough season ; “I'm not really satisfied with it, but I thank God because I've had a very tough season with injuries” ; “Since recovering, every race I've been getting better. This is my third Commonwealth Games. Not everybody gets the opportunity to represent their country three times over twelve years. So I really thank God for that.”

a7027.speaker: Bakary Jammeh, Chief of Mission, Team Gambia
a7027.speech: Expressed appreciation to the Gambian community in Scotland for their hospitality and described the occasion as a reflection of the power of sport to unite people ; “Sports transcends boundaries and brings communities together through a shared passion and common purpose.”

a7027.speaker: Bakary Y. Badjie, Gambian Minister of Youth and Sports
a7027.speech: Commended the Gambian Association in Scotland for the historic initiative and reminded the athletes that they carry the hopes and aspirations of the nation ; “Build on previous Commonwealth Games successes and strive for greater achievements.”

a7027.speaker: Dr Fatou Bensouda, The Gambia's High Commissioner to the United Kingdom
a7027.speech: Described Gambia Day as a celebration of national identity, unity, and excellence ; “Sport continues to serve as a powerful tool for bringing Gambians together, both at home and abroad” ; encouraged the diaspora to keep supporting young people through sport, calling it “a pathway to leadership, education, and national development.”

a7027.speaker: Bai Dodou Jallow, President of the Gambia National Olympic Committee (GNOC)
a7027.speech: Thanked the community for its support, saying such engagement inspires athletes and reminds them they represent a nation united behind them; called on Gambian parents and communities abroad to continue encouraging youth participation in sports, describing investment in youth as an investment in the country's future.

a7027.speaker: Lamin Sanneh, President of the Gambian Association in Glasgow
a7027.speech: Assured Team Gambia of the diaspora's continued support throughout the Games and urged athletes to compete with confidence and pride.

a7027.speaker: Ousman Jobe, Gambian Olympic swimmer
a7027.speech: “There's been some major championships here before, in the 2014 Commonwealth Games as well. I've prepared so well” ; “Plus, two months ago, I was in Paris preparing for this. So I think I'm fully ready.”

a7027.speaker: Pap D. Jonga, Gambian swimmer
a7027.speech: Reflected on Glasgow's world-class facilities and what it will take to develop talent in The Gambia ; “If in The Gambia a supportive system can be created in terms of creating a swimming pool, swimming has a long way to go” ; “Having at least a standard 25-meter pool will enable young kids who are trying to involve themselves in swimming to have big potential for tomorrow.”

a7027.speaker: Pap D. Jonga, Gambian swimmer
a7027.speech: Said the race was a chance to review and improve ; “The performance was great, but it could have been much better. I will use this moment to progress on the few events coming up... to do a review of what went wrong and enable me to have better timing in the races coming up.”

a7027.speaker: King Charles III
a7027.speech: Formally declared the 2026 Commonwealth Games open, alongside Queen Camilla; welcomed the Commonwealth family to Glasgow and praised the city for hosting the event for the fourth time.

a7027.speaker: Confederation of African Football (CAF)
a7027.speech: Now declared Morocco as winners of the AFCON on “disciplinary” grounds after Senegal protested against a penalty decision in the final and left the pitch before coming back to continue playing and ended up winning 1-0 against Morocco.

a7289.speaker: European Union 2023 restrictive-measures regime (official text)
a7289.speech: “In order to guarantee the timely delivery of humanitarian aid or to preserve activities that meet people's basic needs in Niger, the new restrictions regime put in place in 2023 provides for a humanitarian derogation from the asset-freezing measures.”

a7289.speaker: Government of Niger
a7289.speech: Asks on what grounds humanitarian resources are directed toward NGOs chosen by the EU.

a7289.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU foreign policy chief
a7289.speech: “The EU condemned, from the outset, in the strongest terms the coup d'Etat perpetrated in Niger” ; “The EU is sending a clear message: military coups have a cost.”

a7289.speaker: Andrew Lebovich (recent note/analysis)
a7289.speech: In a recent note, Andrew Lebovich evokes the professionalism of the Nigerien army and the failure of cooperation with Eucap owing to the arrogant attitude of the EU's obsolete cooperation system.

a7303.speaker: US State Department (memorandum obtained by Reuters)
a7303.speech: According to the memorandum, the objective is to assess the effectiveness and consistency of US foreign policy; the memorandum mentions specific exemptions, such as military financing for Israel and Egypt, as well as emergency food assistance.

a7303.speaker: Kyeh Kim, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a7303.speech: Said last October that the MCC's third compact, aimed at promoting strategic investments in sectors such as land, air, maritime, digital and human connectivity and mobility, should be signed in April 2026.

a7355.speaker: A Jan. 20 Instagram post
a7355.speech: claims U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE, is offering money for reporting people who are living in the country illegally: “BREAKING: ICE is allegedly offering $750 per illegal immigrant that you turn in through their tip form”… “You can call the ICE hotline at 866-DHS-2-ICE – 866-347-2423.”

a7355.speaker: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
a7355.speech: the agency said it doesn’t offer rewards for aiding in immigration enforcement.

a7355.speaker: ICE spokesperson (anonymous)
a7355.speech: told USA TODAY, “ICE does not offer rewards for tips in support of civil immigration enforcement objectives.”

a7355.speaker: ICE online tip page (website)
a7355.speech: the online tip page states: “Although there is absolutely no guarantee that tip information provided will result in monetary payments, ICE has the discretion and statutory authorization to pay for information and/or evidence that is used in support of criminal investigations.”

a7355.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7355.speech: promised to carry out “mass deportation” after taking office; among the many executive orders he issued during the first day of his second term were a declaration of emergency at the southern border and a call to the military to assist in securing it.

a7355.speaker: News reports from Seattle PI (2016) and ABC News (2018)
a7355.speech: Similar false claims have circulated in the past on stickers and flyers in communities, according to news reports from Seattle PI in 2016 and ABC News in 2018.

a7355.speaker: The Instagram user who shared the post
a7355.speech: USA TODAY reached out to the user who shared the post for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

a7374.speaker: Spokesperson for the French national gendarmerie
a7374.speech: "We are looking into the likelihood of a fire being started deliberately," a spokesperson said on Saturday, adding that no arrests had been made at this stage.

a7374.speaker: Police sources (anonymous)
a7374.speech: Said the outage was caused by an overnight fire, probably an arson attack, at a high-voltage substation in the village of Tanneron, which supplies Cannes.

a7374.speaker: Prosecutors and local officials
a7374.speech: Later confirmed that both the Tanneron power substation and an electricity pylon in Villeneuve-Loubet were vandalised overnight.

a7374.speaker: Local authority for the Alpes-Maritimes region
a7374.speech: Had said earlier on Saturday that the western part of the area, which includes Cannes, was suffering from a major electricity outage.

a7374.speaker: RTE
a7374.speech: According to RTE, while Spain and Portugal suffered blackouts last month, the French Basque Country saw brief power outages with interruptions lasting only a few minutes.

a7374.speaker: Cannes Film Festival organisers
a7374.speech: Said earlier that they had switched to an alternative electricity supply, which enabled them to "maintain the events and screenings planned for today in normal conditions, including the closing ceremony".

a7374.speaker: Cannes Film Festival organisers
a7374.speech: According to the organisers, more than 900 actors and filmmakers signed an open letter denouncing the genocide in Gaza.

a7374.speaker: Open letter signed by more than 900 actors and filmmakers
